query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of phosphorus to high-entropy alloys will improve their glass-forming ability and thermal stability of the amorphous state.
generation.conditions: Varied cooling rates, including slow cooling, accelerated cooling, and rapid quenching using melt-spinning
generation.mechanism: Phosphorus addition enhances glass-forming ability by increasing configurational entropy, leading to improved thermal stability of the amorphous state
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved glass-forming ability and thermal stability of the amorphous state in phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism by which phosphorus addition improves glass-forming ability and thermal stability is not fully understood

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the glass-forming ability and thermal stability of high-entropy alloys with and without phosphorus addition under varied cooling rates
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of phosphorus does not improve glass-forming ability and thermal stability of the amorphous state, the hypothesis is falsified
